mentions.heading: Major disasters or geopolitical conflicts may damage facilities or halt production
mentions.detail: Earthquakes, floods, climate events, geopolitical conflicts affecting facilities or supply chain; fragment of prior risk factor
mentions.quote: We may incur expenses or delays relating to such events outside of our control, which could have a material adverse impact on our business, operating results and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Demand may be impacted by status of government and economic incentives
mentions.detail: Repeal/restriction of consumer, manufacturing and charging infrastructure EV tax credits and regulatory credit programs; domestic-content incentives may exclude Tesla
mentions.quote: Specifically, recent governmental and regulatory actions have repealed and/or restricted consumer, manufacturing and charging infrastructure tax credits, and certain regulatory credit programs tied to our products.

mentions.heading: Demand may be impacted by status of government and economic incentives
mentions.detail: OBBBA requires traceability of raw materials; failure to verify critical mineral origin could lose tax credit eligibility for products
mentions.quote: Compliance with evolving legislation, such as the OBBBA, also requires rigorous traceability of raw materials. If we or our suppliers are unable to provide sufficient documentation to verify the origin of critical minerals, our products may lose eligibility for tax credits and incentives, directly increasing the effective price for our customers and potentially reducing demand.

mentions.heading: Demand may be impacted by status of government and economic incentives
mentions.detail: Net metering reduced or eliminated in several jurisdictions, contested before FERC; hurts solar/storage financing funds and cost of capital
mentions.quote: The benefit available under net metering has been or has been proposed to be reduced, altered or eliminated in several jurisdictions, and has also been contested and may continue to be contested before the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

mentions.heading: Evolving laws and regulations could impose substantial costs or prohibitions
mentions.detail: EHS laws across U.S., China, Germany covering hazardous materials, facilities; climate law changes may raise compliance and remediation costs
mentions.quote: Our business operations are and will continue to be subject to complex environmental, occupational, health and safety laws and regulations at numerous jurisdictional levels in the U.S., China, Germany and other locations abroad, including laws relating to the use, handling, storage, recycling, disposal and/or human exposure to hazardous materials, product material inputs and post-consumer products and with respect to constructing, expanding and maintaining our facilities and other infrastructure.

mentions.heading: Evolving laws and regulations could impose substantial costs or prohibitions
mentions.detail: Increased scrutiny from expanded operations, including litigation and government investigations, could harm brand and talent retention
mentions.quote: In addition, as we have increased our operations, we are and may continue to be subject to increased scrutiny, including litigation and government investigations, that we will need to defend against.

mentions.heading: Evolving laws and regulations could impose substantial costs or prohibitions
mentions.detail: Non-U.S. vehicle safety, fuel economy and emissions standards differ materially, requiring additional vehicle investment and certification
mentions.quote: For example, in countries outside of the U.S., we are required to meet standards relating to vehicle safety, fuel economy and emissions that are often materially different from equivalent requirements in the U.S., thus resulting in additional investment into the vehicles and systems to aim to ensure regulatory compliance in all countries.

drivers.name: vehicle safety, fuel economy and emissions standards
